verdict: BlackRock's revenue rose 19% to $7.8B as markets and $205B of new client money lifted fees, though a $564M noncash deal charge held GAAP operating profit to $2.3B.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Revenue was $7.8B, vs $6.5B a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $8.43 a year ago; as adjusted, $15.93

kpis.label: Net inflows
kpis.note: New client money in the quarter; $869B over 12 months

segments.name: Investment advisory, administration & securities lending
segments.note: The core fees clients pay BlackRock to manage their money, plus securities lending — up 20% on higher markets and strong organic growth in the asset base.

segments.name: Performance fees
segments.note: Extra fees earned when funds beat their targets — up 22%, helped by a large liquid-alternatives fund whose measurement year ends in Q3.

segments.name: Technology services & subscriptions
segments.note: Aladdin risk software and Preqin data subscriptions — up 14%, with annual contract value up 12%.

segments.name: Distribution fees
segments.note: Fees for distributing funds through banks and other sellers — up 17% with the asset base.

segments.name: Advisory & other revenue
segments.note: Advisory work and other smaller revenue lines.

opex.name: Employee compensation & benefits
opex.note: Pay for BlackRock's people — its biggest cost, up just 4% YoY despite the bigger asset base.

opex.name: Direct fund expense
opex.note: The direct cost of running the funds themselves.

opex.name: Sub-advisory & other
opex.note: Fees paid to outside sub-advisers and similar costs.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — offices, technology and professional services.

opex.name: Change in fair value of contingent consideration
opex.note: A noncash charge: the amount BlackRock may still owe for past acquisitions (GIP and HPS) rose in value with its share price. See one-time items.

opex.name: Amortization of intangible assets
opex.note: Spreading the cost of businesses and technology bought in past deals.

follow100.label: Change in fair value of contingent consideration

otherDetail: Nonoperating income was $316M, net: a $353M net gain on investments, less $37M of net interest expense.
footerNote: Distribution and servicing costs — what BlackRock pays the banks and platforms that sell its funds — are shown as the cost of revenue, the closest direct-cost line in its accounts. Net income of $1,920M is before $261M attributable to noncontrolling interests; net income attributable to BlackRock was $1,659M.
oneTimers: A $564M noncash increase in the fair value of contingent consideration — money potentially still owed for the GIP and HPS acquisitions, which rises and falls with BlackRock's share price. It was $93M a year ago.

Acquisition-related costs excluded from the company's adjusted results also included $276M of intangible amortization, $84M of acquisition-related compensation and $46M of acquisition-related admin costs.
Excluding these items, as-adjusted operating income was $3,330M (a 47.8% margin, vs 30.0% GAAP) and adjusted EPS was $15.93, vs $10.57 GAAP.

takeaways.title: Clients poured in money
takeaways.text: Clients added a net $205B in the quarter and $869B over twelve months, taking assets under management to $15.5 trillion. iShares ETFs alone took in $135B, and annualized organic base-fee growth was 11%.

takeaways.title: A deal charge flattened the margin
takeaways.text: GAAP operating margin was 30.0% — the same as a year ago — because of the $564M contingent-consideration charge. Without deal-related items, the adjusted margin was 47.8%, up from 44.6%.

takeaways.title: Technology keeps growing
takeaways.text: Technology services and subscription revenue rose 14% to $588M on Aladdin and Preqin demand, and annual contract value grew 12% — a smaller, steadier business beside the market-driven fees.
